**What we concluded last time**
- **Total group exposure: $344.3M.** That is $308.0M of loan commitments across 10 active facilities plus $36.3M of capital-markets exposure. The group has 24 entities under Halvorsen Industrial Group Inc (LE-10001).
- That is **114.8% of the $300M group house limit ($44.3M over)** and $15.7M below the $360M legal lending limit.
- The downgrade took the group to **internal rating 8 (Substandard)**. All 10 facilities were still booked at rating 5 and had to be re-rated within 5 business days.
- Rating-trigger covenants on **F0000003 and F0000007** were breached.
- Because the rating is 8 or worse and exposure is over the house limit, any credit action needs the **Senior Credit Committee**, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer.

**Has the external rating changed? No.** These are all the rating actions on record for the parent (LE-10001):

| Agency | Earlier rating | Latest rating | Date | Outlook |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agency 1 | BB- (2025-04-15) | **CCC+** | 2026-09-28 | Negative |
| Agency 2 | BB (2025-02-10) | **B** | 2026-06-10 | Negative |

The 2026-09-28 Agency 1 downgrade was already in last time's answer, and nothing has been recorded since. The group rating is the lower of the two agency ratings, so it is still CCC+, which maps to **internal rating 8**.

**Check against current data (2026-09-30)**
- Loan commitments are unchanged: 10 active facilities, **$308.0M**.
- Capital-markets exposure is **$36.3M**, compared with $36.0M in August and $37.9M in July.
- **All 10 facilities are still booked at internal rating 5.** The re-rating to 8 is still outstanding. Five business days from 2026-09-28 gives a deadline of about **2026-10-05**, so it needs to be done now.
- Guarantees don't change the limit position. The parent's guarantee on F0000007 and the guarantee from Halvorsen North America Holdings on F0000003 come from inside the group, so they don't reduce exposure. The only eligible guarantee is Northcastle Mutual Insurance Co's $30M on F0000008 (rated A+ by Agency 1). Even after deducting it, exposure would be about $314.3M, still over the $300M limit.
